explanation: Breadth-first search the starting cell’s same-color component. Flip a cell when it is enqueued so it cannot be enqueued twice, and explore only horizontal and vertical neighbors of its original color.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Only cells matching the starting original color are enqueued, and each is flipped before enqueuing. That flip marks it visited, so no cell is processed twice. Four-neighbor expansion reaches exactly the starting component and changes no differently colored or disconnected cell.
walkthrough: For start (0,0) in [[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[1,0,0]], the connected 1 cells are (0,0),(0,1),(1,1). Flipping them gives [[0,0,0],[0,0,0],[1,0,0]]; the isolated 1 at (2,0) remains.
edgeCases: Diagonal contact alone does not connect cells.
An isolated starting pixel is still flipped.
The starting value determines the component before any recoloring.
